title: Taiwan: A Growing Economic Partner for the E.U. in Troubled Times
text:
Taiwan: A Growing Economic Partner for the E.U. in Troubled Times

The Diplomat

MARVIN RECINOS/AFP via Getty Images

The following excerpt is from an op-ed published in The Diplomat on August 25, 2026, written by Jun-Rong Lin, a policy analyst at Taiwan's Institute for National Defense and Security Research, and Philippe Le Corre, Senior Fellow on Foreign Policy at ASPI's Center for China Analysis.Much has changed since September 2021, when the European Union launched its Indo-Pacific strategy. In less than five years, armed conflicts in Ukraine and in the Middle East have shocked Europeans who know they can no longer fully rely on the close protection of their traditional ally, the United States. Although the U.S. remains NATO’s largest military power, Washington’s recent signs and messages have brought confusion to Europe. In some ways, East Asia faces a similar situation, where Japan and South Korea are now looking at diversification options.Meanwhile, the EU is trying to “pivot” toward Asia, and has developed multiple ties with Japan, India, South Korea, and ASEAN. In that context, Taiwan remains a special case due to its unique situation as the world’s premier producer of high-end semiconductors. As Europe seeks to diversify supply chains and reduce vulnerabilities in strategically important sectors, Taiwan’s comparative advantages have become increasingly aligned with European interests.Within this broader transformation, Taiwan has emerged as a significantly more important partner for the EU than at any previous point since diplomatic relations between the EU and the People’s Republic of China were established, 41 years ago. Once viewed primarily as a trading partner constrained by the EU’s adherence to the “One China” policy, Taiwan has increasingly been incorporated into European discussions on semiconductor resilience, critical technologies, cybersecurity, digital governance, and Indo-Pacific stability. Read the full op-ed here.
